source_refs.note: Book p. 22: 2.1.1 Definition (function, domain, range, codomain; sets of real numbers).
Book p. 23: the pink Note box (co-domain vs range) printed at the top of the page belongs to 2.1.1. Tables, Teaching notes, Key points and Common mistake are ours.

blocks.text: Pichle hisse (2.1) mein hum ne function ka idea roz marra ki misaalon se samjha tha. Ab us idea ko mathematics ki zabaan mein, yani sets ki madad se, baqaida likhte hain. Is hisse mein teen naye alfaaz aayenge: domain, range aur codomain. Inhein achhi tarah samajh lein, kyun ke poore unit mein, balke aage calculus tak, yeh har jagah aate hain.

Kitab ki definition: set \(X\) se set \(Y\) tak function \(f\) ek aisa rule ya correspondence hai jo \(X\) ke har element \(x\) ko \(Y\) ka ek unique (sirf ek, akela) element \(y\) deta hai. Set \(X\) ko \(f\) ka domain kehte hain.

\(Y\) ke jo elements \(y\) is tarah output ke tor par milte hain, un ke set ko \(f\) ki range kehte hain. Aur function ka codomain woh set \(Y\) hai jis ke andar function ki output values (range) parhti hain.
Jab tak kuch aur na kaha jaye, aage hum yeh maan kar chalenge ke sets \(X\) aur \(Y\) real numbers ke sets hain. Yani inputs bhi real numbers aur outputs bhi real numbers.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Co-domain tamam mumkin (possible) outputs ka set hai, lekin range woh outputs hain jo diye gaye domain par function asal mein paida karta hai. Is liye range hamesha co-domain ka subset (hissa) hoti hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Set \(X\) se \(Y\) tak function ko \(f : X \to Y\) likhte hain aur parhte hain "\(f\) from \(X\) to \(Y\)". Teen sets ko ek school ki misaal se samjhiye:
Domain \(X\): woh tamam inputs jo hum use kar sakte hain. Jaise class ke tamam students.
Co-domain \(Y\): woh set jahan outputs ko jaane ki ijazat hai; yeh function banate waqt hi chun liya jata hai. Jaise 1 se 100 tak tamam marks.
Range: woh outputs jo waqai aaye. Jaise students ne asal mein jo marks liye, maslan sirf 45 se 92 tak ke kuch numbers.
Is liye hamesha range \(\subseteq\) co-domain. Range dhoondne ke liye domain ke har element par \(f\) chala kar dekhna parta hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ab upar wali table ko parhte hain. Domain \(X = \{1, 2, 3\}\) ke har element ka bilkul ek output hai: \(1\) ka \(1\), \(2\) ka \(4\), \(3\) ka \(9\). Is liye \(f\), \(X\) se \(Y\) tak function hai.
Domain \(= \{1, 2, 3\}\)
Co-domain \(= Y = \{1, 4, 9, 16\}\)
Range \(= \{1, 4, 9\}\)
Dekhiye, \(16\) co-domain mein to hai, lekin koi input use paida nahin karta (\(16\) ke liye \(x = 4\) chahiye tha jo domain mein hai hi nahin). Is liye \(16\) range mein nahin. Yahi woh farq hai jo Note batata hai: co-domain mein "jagah" hai, range mein sirf "jo waqai pahuncha".

rows: har input ka ek output hai (do inputs ka \(b\) par milna jaiz hai)
blocks.caption: Hamari misaalein: \(Y = \{a, b, c\}\) ke saath definition ko test karna

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is table ki teeno lines ko ek ek kar ke dekhte hain, kyun ke yahi definition ka asal imtihaan hai.
Pehli line: \(2\) aur \(3\) dono \(b\) par ja rahe hain. Kayi students ko lagta hai yeh ghalat hai, lekin definition sirf yeh kehti hai ke har input ka ek output ho. Do inputs ka ek hi output hona bilkul jaiz hai. Is liye yeh function hai. (Note karein: \(c\) kisi ka output nahin, to range \(\{a, b\}\) hai.)
Doosri line: \(1\) ke do outputs \(a\) aur \(b\). "Sirf ek" wali shart toot gayi, is liye function nahin.
Teesri line: \(3\) ka koi output hi nahin. "Har element" wali shart toot gayi, is liye function nahin.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(X = \{-1, 0, 1\}\), \(Y = \{0, 1, 2\}\) aur \(f(x) = x^{2}\). Domain, co-domain aur range kya hain?
Jawab: \(f(-1) = 1\), \(f(0) = 0\), \(f(1) = 1\). Domain \(= \{-1, 0, 1\}\), co-domain \(= \{0, 1, 2\}\), range \(= \{0, 1\}\). Yahan \(-1\) aur \(1\) dono ka output \(1\) hai, phir bhi yeh function hai; aur \(2\) range mein nahin aaya.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Jab sawal ho "kya yeh function hai?", to domain par dono sharten ek ek kar ke check karein: (1) har input ka output hai? (2) kisi input ke do outputs to nahin? Jawab mein woh khaas input zaroor likhein jis par shart toot rahi hai, maslan "function nahin, kyun ke \(1\) ki do images \(a\) aur \(b\) hain". Sirf "nahin" likhne se poore marks nahin milte.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(f : X \to Y\) har \(x \in X\) ko \(Y\) ka ek unique \(y\) deta hai.
2. Domain = inputs ka set \(X\).
3. Co-domain = set \(Y\) jahan outputs ja sakte hain.
4. Range = woh outputs jo waqai bante hain; range \(\subseteq\) co-domain.
5. Is kitab mein \(X\) aur \(Y\) real numbers ke sets hain, jab tak kuch aur na kaha jaye.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Range poocha jaye aur co-domain likh dena. Range mein sirf woh outputs aate hain jo waqai bante hain; is liye har input par \(f\) chala kar dekhein.
2. Yeh samajhna ke \(Y\) ka har element use hona chahiye. Sirf \(X\) ka har element use hona zaroori hai; \(Y\) ke kuch elements khaali reh sakte hain.
3. Kisi rule ko function keh dena jab domain ke kisi element ka output hi na ho.
4. Do inputs ke ek hi output ko ghalat samajhna. Yeh bilkul jaiz hai.
